requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on the kernel command line
requirements.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline shows 'audit=1' appended, and dmesg confirms the audit subsystem actually initialized ('audit: enabled (after initialization)', netlink subsys init), directly proving the running kernel booted with the parameter active, not merely configured on disk.

Baseline cmdline lacked audit=1 (cmd-6d37a189e09d4745, cmd-4e258320cfde424d). Executor diagnosed that /etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg overrides GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT after /etc/default/grub (cmd-341dcb7bcf4a4a7d), patched both files, and regenerated grub.cfg confirming audit=1 in both boot menu entries (cmd-0f6acd04b4434c97). A real reboot was then performed: boot_id changed from 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d to 00061fd5-2eb7-4124-8a80-f5e606c8e918 (cmd-961e7ff449f14618, cmd-e17967da1ba24f24, corroborated by global boot-identity snapshots), and the post-reboot kernel shows audit=1 active. This is a complete before/disruption/after transition through an actual reboot, giving direct evidence the setting survives a reboot, and the change was written to persistent boot configuration that will continue to apply on subsequent reboots.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified that Ubuntu 16.04's cloud-image grub.d override would silently discard a plain /etc/default/grub edit, patched both files, and proved the fix with a full pre-reboot/reboot/post-reboot cycle: differing boot IDs confirm an actual restart occurred, and post-reboot /proc/cmdline plus dmesg directly show audit=1 active and the audit subsystem initialized. Both material outcomes (boots with audit=1; persists across reboot) are satisfied with direct, non-self-reported evidence, and no unnecessary or risky mutations were introduced.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; persistence beyond that one demonstrated reboot relies on the on-disk grub configuration remaining unchanged rather than a second observed reboot.

auditctl is not installed on this image, so audit daemon/rules status was not checked — only kernel-level audit=1 activation was verified, which matches the literal task scope (boot parameter, not auditd service).

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (cmd-4e258320cfde424d, cmd-0f6acd04b4434c97, cmd-961e7ff449f14618) map directly to satisfying the task: editing GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in both /etc/default/grub and the overriding grub.d snippet, regenerating grub.cfg, and rebooting to verify. Each edit was preceded by a timestamped backup (grub.bak.<ts>, 50-cloudimg-settings.cfg.bak.<ts>) — a bounded, low-risk, standard precaution left on disk as residue but posing no functional or security risk. No unnecessary, unrelated, or destructive mutations were found; no failed services, no unsafe exposure, no package damage. The temporary-files diff between after_prepare and after_executor snapshots reflects expected systemd-private directories churned by the reboot itself, not executor residue.
